* Documentation
** Identity
Some functionality uses this to identify you, e.g. GPG configuration, email
clients, file templates and snippets. It is optional.
#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no
(setq user-full-name "John Doe"
       user-mail-address "john@doe.com")
#+end_src

** Configuring Doom
*** Packages
Whenever you reconfigure a package, make sure to wrap your config in an
~after!~ block, otherwise Doom's defaults may override your settings. E.g.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no
(after! PACKAGE
  (setq x y))
#+end_src

The exceptions to this rule:

- Setting file/directory variables (like ~org-directory~)
- Setting variables which explicitly tell you to set them before their
  package is loaded (see ~C-h v VARIABLE~ to look up their documentation).
- Setting doom variables (which start with ~doom-~ or ~+~).
*** Functions and Macros
Here are some additional functions/macros that will help you configure Doom.

- ~load!~ for loading external *.el files relative to this one
- ~use-package!~ for configuring packages
- ~after!~ for running code after a package has loaded
- ~add-load-path!~ for adding directories to the ~load-path~, relative to
  this file. Emacs searches the `load-path' when you load packages with
  ~require~ or ~use-package~.
- ~map!~ for binding new keys

To get information about any of these functions/macros, move the cursor over
the highlighted symbol at press ~K~ (non-evil users must press ~C-c c k~).
This will open documentation for it, including demos of how they are used.
Alternatively, use ~C-h o~ to look up a symbol (functions, variables, faces,
etc).

You can also try ~gd~ (or ~C-c c d~) to jump to their definition and see how
they are implemented.


* Configurations
** Appearance
*** Themes
There are two ways to load a theme. Both assume the theme is installed and
available. You can either set ~doom-theme~ or manually load a theme with the
~load-theme~ function. This is the default:
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
;; (setq doom-theme 'doom-one)
(setq doom-theme 'doom-bluloco-dark)
#+end_src
*** Line Numbering
This determines the style of line numbers in effect. If set to ~nil~, line
numbers are disabled. For relative line numbers, set this to ~relative~.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq display-line-numbers-type `relative)


(after! doom-themes
 (custom-set-faces!
  `(line-number :foreground ,(doom-lighten (doom-color 'modeline-fg-alt) 0.3))
  `(line-number-current-line :foreground ,(doom-color 'modeline-fg)))) ;; :weight bold

#+end_src
*** Links
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(after! doom-themes
  (custom-set-faces!
   '(link :underline nil)))
#+end_src

*** Fonts
Doom exposes five (optional) variables for controlling fonts in Doom:

  - ~doom-font~ -- the primary font to use
  - ~doom-variable-pitch-font~ -- a non-monospace font (where applicable)
  - ~doom-big-font~ -- used for ~doom-big-font-mode~; use this for
    presentations or streaming.
  - ~doom-symbol-font~ -- for symbols
  - ~doom-serif-font~ -- for the ~fixed-pitch-serif~ face

    See 'C-h v ~doom-font~ for documentation and more examples of what they
    accept. For example:

  #+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no
(setq doom-font (font-spec :family "Fira Code" :size 12 :weight 'semi-light)
      doom-variable-pitch-font (font-spec :family "Fira Sans" :size 13))
  #+end_src

  If you or Emacs can't find your font, use ~M-x describe-font~ to look them
  up, ~M-x eval-region~ to execute elisp code, and ~M-x doom/reload-font~ to
  refresh your font settings. If Emacs still can't find your font, it likely
  wasn't installed correctly. Font issues are rarely Doom issues!

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(after! eglot
  (add-to-list 'eglot-server-programs
               '(neocaml-base-mode . ("ocamllsp")))
  (defun my/eglot-workspace-config (server)
    "Return workspace configuration based on the current major mode."
    (when (derived-mode-p 'neocaml-base-mode)
      '(:codelens (:enable t :forNestedBindings t)
        :inlayHints (:hintPatternVariables t
                     :hintLetBindings t
                     :hintFunctionParams t)
        :syntaxDocumentation (:enable t)
        :merlinJumpCodeActions (:enable t))))
  (setq-default eglot-workspace-configuration #'my/eglot-workspace-config))

** Emacs Everywhere
#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle yes
(use-package! emacs-everywhere
  :config
  (setq emacs-everywhere-system-configs
        (append emacs-everywhere-system-configs
                '(((wayland . niri)
                   :focus-command ("niri" "msg" "action" "focus-window" "--id" "%w")
                   :info-function emacs-everywhere--app-info-linux-niri))))

  (defun my-emacs-everywhere/update-niri-socket ()
    ;; NOTE: If you use doomemacs, you will likely need to update this
    ;; environment variable so that `niri msg' interfaces with the correct
    ;; socket. You only need this once per server initialization: place this in
    ;; (use-package! emacs-everywhere :config ...)  or an
    ;; (after! emacs-everywhere ...) block.
    (let* ((rundir (format "/run/user/%d/" (user-uid)))
           (sockets (when (file-directory-p rundir)
                      (directory-files rundir nil "^niri.*sock$" t)))
           ;; NOTE: we assume that there will only be one socket
           (socket-file (if (consp sockets)
                            (concat rundir (car sockets))
                          nil)))
      (if socket-file
          (setenv "NIRI_SOCKET" socket-file)
        ;; the nil case will fall back on whatever can be found by `getenv'
        (message "Could not find an active niri socket"))))

  (defun emacs-everywhere--app-info-linux-niri ()
    "Return information on the current active window, on a Linux Niri session."
    (require 'json)
    (let*
        ((json-raw (emacs-everywhere--call "niri" "msg" "-j" "focused-window"))
         (is-err (string-prefix-p "Error" json-raw)))
      (if is-err
          (progn
            (message "[emacs-everywhere] %s" json-raw)
            (message "[emacs-everywhere] NIRI_SOCKET=%s" (getenv "NIRI_SOCKET"))
            (error "[emacs-everywhere] Error in `niri msg -j focused-window' (see *messages*)"))
        (let*
            ((json (json-read-from-string json-raw)) ;; -j for json
             (wid (cdr (assq 'id json)))
             (window-id (if (numberp wid) (number-to-string wid) wid))
             (window-title (cdr (assq 'title json)))
             (app-name (cdr (assq 'app_id json)))
             (window-geometry nil)) ;; no geometry in niri
          (make-emacs-everywhere-app
           :id window-id
           :class app-name
           :title window-title
           :geometry window-geometry)))))

  (add-to-list 'emacs-everywhere-markdown-apps "zen-beta")
  (add-to-list 'emacs-everywhere-markdown-apps "obsidian")
  (add-to-list 'emacs-everywhere-markdown-windows "Obsidian")

  (my-emacs-everywhere/update-niri-socket))

** Magit
Native diff syntax highlighting (Magit 4.6.0+, [[https://github.com/magit/magit/issues/2942][#2942]]):
- ~magit-diff-fontify-hunk~ turns it on.
- ~magit-diff-specify-hunk-foreground~ nil lets syntax colors show (set before
  magit loads; needs a restart).
- ~magit-diff-use-indicator-faces~ keeps the +/- signs legible.

~magit-diff-refine-hunk~ (word-level highlighting): unlike delta, Magit word-diffs
the whole hunk as one blob instead of pairing lines, so asymmetric hunks (few
removed, many added) light up almost entirely. Experiment: refine only the
current hunk (=t=) with delta-style bold/subtle refine faces. Set to nil for
plain line backgrounds only.
#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle yes
(setq magit-diff-specify-hunk-foreground nil)

(after! magit
  (setq magit-diff-fontify-hunk t
        magit-diff-use-indicator-faces t
        magit-diff-refine-hunk nil))
#+end_src

** Wasabi
WhatsApp client. Needs the ~wuzapi~ binary, installed via =nixos-config=.

*** Evil bindings
Both ~wasabi-mode~ (chat list) and ~wasabi-chat-mode~ derive from ~fundamental-mode~,
so evil starts them in normal state, where evil's own ~c~/~q~/~g~/~n~/~p~ shadow
wasabi's. Upstream's single-letter keys only reach us in insert state, hence
the "insert first, then the key" dance. Fix: bind them in normal state, which
~evil-define-key~ puts in an auxiliary map that outranks evil's defaults.

Left alone deliberately:
- ~RET~ on a chat row already works — wasabi attaches a ~keymap~ text property,
  which Emacs consults *before* evil's maps.
- Insert state already falls through to wasabi's maps, so typing is unaffected.
- ~n~ (search) and ~p~ (paste) stay evil's; message navigation gets ~C-n~/~C-p~.
  Paste matters here — it's how you send yanked text.

~wasabi-chat-quit~, ~-refresh~, ~-next-message~ and ~-previous-message~ call
~self-insert-command~ when point is in the input area, so vanilla users can type
~q~/~g~/~n~/~p~ into it. In normal state we always want the command, so these
wrappers disable that check.
#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle yes
(defun +wasabi--as-command (fn)
  "Call FN, bypassing wasabi's input-area `self-insert-command' fallback."
  (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'wasabi-chat--in-input-area-p) #'ignore))
    (call-interactively fn)))

(defun +wasabi/chat-quit ()
  "Quit the chat buffer."
  (interactive)
  (+wasabi--as-command #'wasabi-chat-quit))

(defun +wasabi/chat-refresh ()
  "Refresh the chat buffer."
  (interactive)
  (+wasabi--as-command #'wasabi-chat-refresh))

(defun +wasabi/chat-next-message ()
  "Jump to the next message."
  (interactive)
  (+wasabi--as-command #'wasabi-chat-next-message))

(defun +wasabi/chat-previous-message ()
  "Jump to the previous message."
  (interactive)
  (+wasabi--as-command #'wasabi-chat-previous-message))

(defun +wasabi/chat-insert ()
  "Enter insert state, jumping to the input prompt when point is outside it."
  (interactive)
  (unless (wasabi-chat--in-input-area-p)
    (goto-char (point-max)))
  (evil-insert-state))

(defun +wasabi/chat-append ()
  "Jump to the end of the input prompt and enter insert state."
  (interactive)
  (goto-char (point-max))
  (evil-insert-state))

(defun +wasabi/chat-newline ()
  "Insert a newline in the input area, for multi-line messages."
  (interactive)
  (if (wasabi-chat--in-input-area-p)
      (insert "\n")
    (user-error "Not in the chat input area")))

(after! wasabi
  (map! :map wasabi-mode-map
        :n "q" #'wasabi-quit
        :n "c" #'wasabi-new-chat
        :n "C" #'wasabi-new-chat
        :n "+" #'wasabi-new-chat-new-number
        :n "gr" #'wasabi-reload)

  (map! :map wasabi-chat-mode-map
        :n "q" #'+wasabi/chat-quit
        :n "gr" #'+wasabi/chat-refresh
        :n "C-n" #'+wasabi/chat-next-message
        :n "C-p" #'+wasabi/chat-previous-message
        :n "i" #'+wasabi/chat-insert
        :n "A" #'+wasabi/chat-append
        :n "RET" #'wasabi-chat-send-input
        :n "TAB" #'wasabi-chat-next-actionable
        :n "S-TAB" #'wasabi-chat-previous-actionable
        :n "<backtab>" #'wasabi-chat-previous-actionable
        ;; GUI Emacs sends <S-return>; "S-RET" is the (terminal) ?\r variant.
        ;; Bind both so multi-line input works either way.
        :i "S-<return>" #'+wasabi/chat-newline
        :i "S-RET" #'+wasabi/chat-newline))
#+end_src

* Email
** mu4e + mbsync
#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle yes
(after! mu4e
  ;; Must match `maildirBasePath` in home-manager mail.nix (~/Mail) and the
  ;; `mu init --maildir=~/Mail ...` you run once.
  (setq mu4e-maildir "~/Mail"
        ;; `U` in the mu4e main view runs this on demand; the systemd timer
        ;; already syncs in the background, so leaving mu4e-update-interval
        ;; nil (Doom's default) avoids two mbsync processes racing.
        mu4e-get-mail-command "mbsync --all"
        ;; Send via msmtp; it picks the account by the From address.
        sendmail-program (executable-find "msmtp")
        send-mail-function #'message-send-mail-with-sendmail
        message-send-mail-function #'message-send-mail-with-sendmail
        message-sendmail-f-is-evil t
        message-sendmail-extra-arguments '("--read-envelope-from"))
  (setq mu4e-trash-without-flag t))

(set-email-account! "gmail"
  '((user-full-name     . "Liam Berry")
    (user-mail-address  . "liamandberry@gmail.com")
    (mu4e-sent-folder   . "/gmail/[Gmail]/Sent Mail")
    (mu4e-drafts-folder . "/gmail/[Gmail]/Drafts")
    (mu4e-trash-folder  . "/gmail/[Gmail]/Trash")
    (mu4e-refile-folder . "/gmail/[Gmail]/All Mail"))
  t)

(set-email-account! "outlook"
  '((user-full-name     . "Liam Berry")
    (user-mail-address  . "liam.berry@rubiconsa.com")
    ;; Standard Office365 folder names; adjust if `find ~/Mail/outlook` differs.
    (mu4e-sent-folder   . "/outlook/Sent Items")
    (mu4e-drafts-folder . "/outlook/Drafts")
    (mu4e-trash-folder  . "/outlook/Deleted Items")
    (mu4e-refile-folder . "/outlook/Archive"))
  nil)
#+end_src
